title: Why Do Your Ears Pop When You Fly?
hook: Why do your ears pop when you fly in an aeroplane?

narration.text: Your ears pop because of changing air pressure.
This pressure difference occurs when you change altitude.
Inside your ear is a small tube called the Eustachian tube.
It connects your middle ear to the back of your throat.
This tube opens and closes to equalise pressure.
That popping sound is just air moving to balance it out.
Try swallowing or yawning next time your ears feel blocked.
Like this if it surprised you, comment with your best plane story, and subscribe for more insights into your amazing body.

description: Ever wondered why your ears pop when you're on a plane or driving up a mountain? It is all about how your body handles changes in air pressure. This short explains the clever mechanism inside your ear that equalises the pressure, making that satisfying pop.
topic: Why your ears might 'pop' when you change altitude, like in an aeroplane. This is your body equalising air pressure.
